text.p: Tambrands Inc shares opened sharply higher on Wednesday, then settled down with a gain of more than five percent, following news of a $46 million restructuring at the company.
The restructuring, which includes closure of four of nine manufacturing plants, spurred at least two analysts to raise their opinions of the stock.
Tambrands was up 2-3/8, or 5.7 percent, to 44-1/8 on the New York Stock Exchange, having backed off from a high of 44-3/4 reached earlier in the session.
J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Grant said in a research note that he raised the stock to a market performer from underperformer because of the restructuring.
The move, expected to wipe out 1,100 jobs, or 17 percent of the workforce, "is expected to reap annual cost savings of roughly $20 million starting in 1998," Grant wrote.

"If all this cost savings were to fall to the bottom line (which we doubt) this would indicate a roughly $0.17 increase to EPS in 1997 (assuming half of the benefit is realized) and a $0.34 increase to EPS starting in 1998," he stated.

"We review Tambrands' restructuring positively. Longer term, however, we remain neutral on Tambrands, as it is a one-category company, and we expect the tampon business is likely to remain ultracompetitive for the foreseeable future," the analyst said."
Also, Morgan Stanley raised its rating on the stock to outperform from neutral.
